newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola's ruling party extends its term.
newsitem.headline: Angola's ruling party extends its term.

text.p: Angola's ruling MPLA has extended its hold on parliament for two to four years with constitutional amendments published in the government gazette on Friday.

The party made the move without consulting its former enemy UNITA, now the MPLA's partner in the peace process. The amendments extend the legislative mandate until political, military and security conditions are in place to hold elections in two to four years.
The move comes ahead of a November 26 expiry for the mandate of the current parliament, which has an overwhelming MPLA majority of 129 seats.
The opposition UNITA won 70 seats in the 1992 elections but failed to occupy them after rejecting results of the poll and returning to war.
The government and UNITA sealed a peace pact in 1994 to end the fighting and are implementing the accord which foresees a unity government and single national army.

Although both sides agreed last year to extend the mandate, UNITA's chief peace negotiator in a joint ceasefire commission, Isaias Smakuva, told Reuters the amendments were passed without consulting UNITA.

"We gave them our proposals last month so as to avoid problems in November when the mandate expires, but they never answered us," Samakuva said. "Last Sunday we received a copy of the current revised law without any of the changes which we had proposed."
He said he raised the issue at a meeting of the joint commission on Monday, but the government appeared unwilling to discuss it.
"I don't believe this will create a block in the further implementation of the peace plan, but it does nothing for confidence building," Samakuva said.
